# Instance

- **Not creatable**: it cannot be created with `Instance.new`
- **Abstract**: it cannot be created; other classes inherit from it

The base class of every object in the tree. An instance has a name, a parent, children, attributes and tags.

This page lists the members this class declares. Inherited members are
listed on the page of the class that declares them.

## Properties

| Name | Type | Default | Access | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `ClassName` | `string` | — | read-only | The name of this instance's class. `typeof` returns `Instance` for every class, so use `ClassName` or `IsA` to tell classes apart. |
| `Local` | `boolean` | — | read-only | Whether this instance exists only on this machine and is never sent to another. It is true for an instance that a client-side script made with `Instance.new` or `Clone`, and for everything under it. A client-side script is one under `ClientScriptService`, in the client half of `GlobalScriptService`, or with a `RunContext` other than `Server`; this applies on a host as well as on a machine that joined.<br><br>Instances made by server-side scripts or loaded from a scene are not local, and replicate. The value records who made the instance, not who writes to it later: a client-side script on a host that sets a property of a replicated instance changes it for every player. |
| `Name` | `string` | — | read/write | The name of this instance. Siblings can share a name. Renaming an instance to a name that a `WaitForChild` call is waiting for resumes that call, as parenting a new child would. |
| `Parent` | `Instance?` | — | read/write | The instance this one is a child of, or nil when it has no parent. Setting it adds this instance after its new siblings. Setting it after `Destroy` raises an error. |
| `Phase` | `string` | `""` | read/write | The phase this instance and everything under it belong to, seen only by the players in it. Empty, the default, is everybody's. A player not in the phase (`Player:AddPhase`) is not sent the instance at all: it is absent on their machine, not hidden. It leaves their machine when they leave the phase, as a thing out of range does. It is the server's to say and is not itself sent.<br><br>A phased part collides with the characters, and the parts, of the players in its phase, and never with those of players who are not; everything else collides with it as with any part (`BasePart.PhaseCollision`). A world names at most 64 phases. |

## Methods

### `AddTag(tag: string)`

Adds a tag to this instance. Does nothing if the instance already has it. Tags do not depend on the tree: an instance with no parent keeps its tags and is still found by them.

### `Clone(): Instance`

Returns a copy of this instance and everything under it, with no parent. Properties, attributes and tags are copied at every depth. A reference to an instance inside the copied tree points to the copy; a reference to anything outside it still points to the original.

### `Destroy()`

Removes this instance and all of its descendants permanently. `Parent` is set to nil and locked, tags are cleared, and `Destroying` fires. The instance remains readable until the `Destroying` handlers have run. After that, `Parent` reads nil and `IsDescendantOf` and `IsAncestorOf` return false, but reading `Name` or `ClassName` or calling `IsA` raises an error.

### `FindFirstAncestor(name: string): Instance?`

Returns the nearest ancestor with the given name, or nil. The search starts at `Parent`; the instance itself is never returned.

### `FindFirstAncestorOfClass(className: string): Instance?`

Returns the nearest ancestor whose `ClassName` is exactly `className`, or nil. The search starts at `Parent`; the instance itself is never returned.

### `FindFirstChild(name: string): Instance?`

Returns the first child with the given name, or nil. Only direct children are searched; to search deeper, loop over `GetDescendants`.

### `FindFirstChildOfClass(className: string): Instance?`

Returns the first child whose `ClassName` is exactly `className`, or nil. Subclasses do not match: asking for `BasePart` never finds a `Part`.

### `FindFirstChildWhichIsA(className: string): Instance?`

Returns the first child that is of the class `className` or of a class derived from it, or nil. Abstract base classes such as `BasePart` are accepted.

### `GetAttribute(name: string): (string | number | boolean | vector | CFrame | Color3 | Vector2 | UDim | UDim2 | Rect | ColorSequence | NumberSequence)?`

Returns the value of the named attribute, or nil if it has never been set. Attribute names are case-sensitive.

### `GetAttributeChangedSignal(name: string): Signal<()>`

Returns a signal that fires when the named attribute changes. The attribute does not have to exist yet.

### `GetAttributes(): { [string]: string | number | boolean | vector | CFrame | Color3 | Vector2 | UDim | UDim2 | Rect | ColorSequence | NumberSequence }`

Returns a new table of this instance's attributes, keyed by name.

### `GetChildren(): {Instance}`

Returns a new array of this instance's children, in the order they were parented. The array is a copy, so it is safe to destroy children while looping over it.

### `GetDescendants(): {Instance}`

Returns a new array of every descendant, depth first: each child, followed by that child's own descendants.

### `GetFullName(): string`

Returns the path to this instance: the names of its ancestors and its own name, joined by dots, such as `Workspace.Tree.Trunk`. The path starts below the data model. It is meant for logs; siblings can share a name, so a path does not always identify one instance.

### `GetPropertyChangedSignal(name: string): Signal<()>`

Returns a signal that fires when the named property changes. The signal passes no arguments; read the property for its new value. Each call returns the same signal. Raises an error if the class has no such property.

### `GetStamp(): string?`

Returns the content path of the stamp this instance was placed from, such as `stamps/fighter.stamp.json`, or nil. Only a linked copy of a stamp returns a path; a copy placed unlinked returns nil. A copy's parameters are stored as its attributes.

### `GetTags(): {string}`

Returns a new array of this instance's tags.

### `HasTag(tag: string): boolean`

Returns whether this instance has the given tag.

### `IsA(className: string): boolean`

Returns whether this instance is of the given class or of a class derived from it. A name that is not a class returns false instead of raising an error.

### `IsAncestorOf(descendant: Instance): boolean`

Returns whether `descendant` is anywhere below this instance. An instance is not its own ancestor. Returns false if either instance has been destroyed.

### `IsDescendantOf(ancestor: Instance): boolean`

Returns whether this instance is anywhere below `ancestor`. An instance is not its own descendant. Returns false if either instance has been destroyed.

### `RemoveTag(tag: string)`

Removes a tag from this instance. Does nothing if the instance does not have it.

### `SetAttribute(name: string, value: (string | number | boolean | vector | CFrame | Color3 | Vector2 | UDim | UDim2 | Rect | ColorSequence | NumberSequence)?)`

Sets the named attribute, or removes it when `value` is nil. Raises an error for a table, an instance or a function, and for an empty name; the previous value is kept.

### `WaitForChild(name: string, timeout: number? = nil): Instance?`

This method yields: the calling thread waits until it completes.

Waits until a child with the given name exists, and returns it. Returns immediately if one already exists. With `timeout`, returns nil when the time runs out. Without one, it waits indefinitely and logs a warning after five seconds of game time.

## Events

Signals are deferred: a handler runs at the next resumption point, not
inside the call that fired the signal.

### `AncestryChanged(instance: Instance, newParent: Instance?)`

Fires when this instance or one of its ancestors is given a new parent. Passes the instance that moved and its new parent, which is nil if it was unparented. It fires on the moved instance first, then on each of its descendants.

### `AttributeChanged(name: string)`

Fires when any attribute of this instance changes. Passes the attribute's name.

### `ChildAdded(child: Instance)`

Fires after an instance becomes a child of this one. Passes the child.

### `ChildRemoved(child: Instance)`

Fires after an instance stops being a child of this one. Passes the child.

### `DescendantAdded(descendant: Instance)`

Fires after an instance is added anywhere below this one. Passes the descendant.

### `DescendantRemoving(descendant: Instance)`

Fires when an instance is removed from anywhere below this one. Passes the descendant. When an instance moves from one parent to another, the removal fires before the addition.

### `Destroying()`

Fires once when `Destroy` is called on this instance. Handlers run after the instance has already been removed from the tree.
